speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you have a painful, ulcerative skin lesion on your leg. To help me determine the cause, can you tell me how long this lesion has been present and if you recall any trauma or insect bite at the site?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Cutaneous Leishmaniasis.

The combination of a single, progressively enlarging ulcerative lesion on the leg following an insect bite (ant), in a patient with significant immunosuppression due to Crohn's disease and a history of corticosteroid use for uveitis, strongly suggests this parasitic infection. I will now request a biopsy and parasite smear for confirmation.
